tEn: From No-Code to ChatGPT Work: The Era of Bottoms-Up Ambition
tZh: 从无代码到 ChatGPT Work：自下而上的雄心时代
sEn: Akshay from OpenAI discusses how ideas and taste are the new bottlenecks, and how ChatGPT Work embodies the mission of bringing code's magic to everyone.
sZh: 来自 OpenAI 的 Akshay 探讨了想法和品味如何成为新的瓶颈，以及 ChatGPT Work 如何体现将代码魔力带给每个人的使命。

consensus.en: The bottleneck for building with AI is ideas and taste, not technical ability, since anyone can build now.
consensus.zh: 用AI构建的瓶颈在于想法和品味，而非技术能力，因为现在谁都能上手构建。

consensus.en: Default model settings should be the best for most users; choices should be simplified, not multiplied.
consensus.zh: 默认模型设置应最适合大多数用户，选项应简化而非增加。

consensus.en: Agents unlock capabilities for everyone, not just developers, as seen by Codex adoption inside OpenAI.
consensus.zh: 智能体为每个人解锁能力，而不仅仅是开发者，OpenAI内部Codex的采用就是例证。

consensus.en: Teams must distinguish motion from progress; real progress needs prescriptive goals rather than proxy metrics.
consensus.zh: 团队必须区分忙碌动作与真正进展；真正进展需要明确的目标，而非替代指标。

consensus.en: Memory and accumulated context make ChatGPT feel personal and are central to its value across products.
consensus.zh: 记忆与积累的上下文让ChatGPT显得个性化，这是其跨产品价值的关键。

consensus.en: Personal and professional productivity are blurring; tools should not box users into rigid roles.
consensus.zh: 个人与职业生产力正在模糊，工具不应把用户束缚在僵化角色里。

contrarian.en: Sites emerged as a knowledge work artifact, replacing slide decks and spreadsheets for internal finance collaboration.
contrarian.zh: Sites已成为知识工作产物，在内部财务协作中取代幻灯片和电子表格。

contrarian.en: LLM-generated performance review context is not slop but agentic search that can surface wins supervisors missed.
contrarian.zh: 用LLM生成绩效评估背景不是垃圾内容，而是智能体式搜索，能找出主管遗漏的亮点。

contrarian.en: More people should use lighter models like Terra, because heavy models like Soul exhaust capacity and may be overkill.
contrarian.zh: 更多人应使用Terra这类轻量模型，因为Soul等重型模型会耗尽算力且可能过度。

contrarian.en: People should re-test capabilities they gave up on months ago; models improve faster than expectations.
contrarian.zh: 人们应重新尝试几个月前放弃的能力；模型进步快于预期。

contrarian.en: We want users not to choose their AGI variant; the product should route them to the right agentic mode automatically.
contrarian.zh: 我们希望用户不用选择自己的AGI版本；产品应自动将他们路由到正确的智能体模式。

contrarian.en: Merging Codex and ChatGPT was counterintuitive but intentional to avoid boxing users into separate product identities.
contrarian.zh: 合并Codex和ChatGPT看似反直觉，但这是为了避免把用户困在分离的产品身份中。

turns.en: I think the bottleneck becomes ideas and taste, I guess. Because anyone can build now, it really is the era of bottoms-up ambition. And because there's so much to be built, you're always going to be bottlenecked by the number of ideas and the number of things you're doing at any given time.
turns.zh: 我觉得瓶颈会变成想法和品味，我猜。因为现在谁都能开发，这真的是自下而上野心的时代。而且因为有太多东西要造，你在任何时候都总会被想法数量和你手头正在做的事情的数量所限制。

turns.en: One interesting part about ideas is that they're not in a vacuum. They usually come from somewhere. In product development, they come from talking to users, or reacting to friction you're seeing, or feedback. There will always be value in these generalists we talked about—closing that loop and coming up with ideas that are grounded in that feedback or from talking to users, whatever it is.
turns.zh: 关于想法，一个有意思的地方是它们不是凭空产生的。它们通常来自某处。在产品开发中，它们来自与用户交谈，或者是对你所见的摩擦的反应，或者是反馈。我们之前谈到的这些通才总有价值——闭合这个回路，并基于这些反馈或与用户的交流来提出想法，无论是什么。

turns.en: Before we get into today's episode, I just have a small message for listeners. Thank you. We wouldn't be able to bring you the AI engineering, science, and entertainment content that you clearly want if you didn't choose to click in and tune into our content. We've been approached by sponsors almost daily, but fortunately enough of you actually subscribe to keep this sustainable without ads, and we want to keep it that way. But I have one favor to ask of you. The single most powerful, completely free thing you can do is click that subscribe button. It's the only thing I'll ever ask of you, and it means absolutely everything to me and my team who work so hard to bring In Space to you each and every week. If you do it, I promise you we'll never stop working to make the show even better. Now, let's get into it.
turns.zh: 在进入今天的节目之前，我先给听众们一个小消息。谢谢你们。如果你们没有选择点进并收听我们的内容，我们就无法为你带来你如此想要的 AI 工程、科学和娱乐内容。几乎每天都有人来找我们谈赞助，但幸运的是，你们中有足够多的人真正订阅了我们，让我们可以在没有广告的情况下维持这一切，而我们希望继续保持这样。但我有一件事想请你们帮忙。你们能做的最有力、完全免费的一件事，就是点击那个订阅按钮。这是我对你们唯一的请求，而这对我来说，以及对我的团队来说，意义重大——他们每周都那么努力地把 In Space 带给你。如果你们订阅了，我保证我们会永不停止地努力把节目做得更好。那么，让我们开始吧。

turns.en: Okay, we're here in the studio with Akshay from OpenAI. Welcome.
turns.zh: 好的，今天我们请到了来自 OpenAI 的 Akshay。欢迎。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: And with our trusty co-host Vibhu. So, you recently launched ChatGPT Work. You lead core product engineering. It's been a long journey into all this. I find it very interesting that you started with no-code or low-code with Walrus and Airtable. And to some extent, ChatGPT Work is kind of like the super app of super apps—well, here is the ultimate no-code, you just write a prompt.
turns.zh: 还有我们可靠的联合主持人 Vibhu。那么，你们最近发布了 ChatGPT Work。你领导核心产品工程。走到今天是一段很长的旅程。我觉得很有意思的是，你最初从 Walrus 和 Airtable 做无代码或低代码起家。而在某种程度上，ChatGPT Work 就像是超级应用中的超级应用——这里就是终极无代码，你只要写一个提示词。

turns.en: Yeah, it's funny how things come full circle. For a long time in my career—I started in consumer fintech—but then there was this hypothesis that the things we could do with code as engineers, if we could bring that to many more people in a more accessible way, would be truly magical. We were working on a startup. I actually worked on automated testing with AI before LLMs, before vision LLMs. It was kind of janky back then, but you do what you can. Then I worked at Airtable for a while on the same thesis: if we can bring a database, or the parameters behind a database, to people, that would be really useful to them. But once LLMs came onto the scene, it became clear that this was the missing piece—the missing technology required to bring the magic of code to everyone without them having to know what's going on under the hood. So I think this launch, and all the stuff we've been up to, is the manifestation of that.
turns.zh: 是的，事情兜兜转转又回到原点，很有意思。在我的职业生涯中有很长一段时间——我从消费金融科技起步——但后来有了一个假设：我们作为工程师能用代码做到的事情，如果能以更容易上手的方式带给更多人，那会非常神奇。我们当时在做一个创业项目。我实际上在 LLM 出现之前、在视觉 LLM 出现之前，就做过用 AI 进行自动化测试。那时候还挺粗糙的，但你只能尽力而为。后来我在 Airtable 工作了一段时间，也是基于同样的论点：如果我们能把数据库、或者说数据库背后的参数带给人们，那对他们会非常有用。但一旦 LLM 出现，就变得很明显：这就是缺失的那一块——把代码的魔力带给每个人、而不需要他们了解底层原理所需的那项关键技术。所以我觉得这次发布，以及我们所做的所有事情，就是那个想法的体现。

turns.en: How was stuff when you joined? You joined OpenAI in 2023. Now we've got so much more stuff: ChatGPT, Codex app, ChatGPT for Work. How have things changed?
turns.zh: 你加入的时候情况如何？你是在 2023 年加入 OpenAI 的。现在我们有了多得多的东西：ChatGPT、Codex 应用、ChatGPT for Work。事情发生了怎样的变化？

turns.en: Actually, I think the more interesting thing is how things haven't changed. I remember when I joined, it was about 500 people. One thing I was worried about was that I was looking for something more early-stage, and wondered if it would be startup-y enough. But when I joined, I was like, dude, this feels even more startup-y than I could ever imagine. And that really hasn't changed even now. The level of bottoms-up ambition, and the ability for anyone to do anything, have an idea, and ship it, is really cool. But on the mission side, what was really compelling to me is this mission of bringing frontier intelligence to everyone—building AGI and then bringing it to everyone. And I think even then we acknowledged that the vision wouldn't be a linear progression. We'll probably try different products and have different things that succeed and don't. But the vision has stayed the same, the mission has stayed the same, and we're starting to see the pieces fall together. That's really cool.
turns.zh: 实际上，我觉得更有意思的是事情没有变的地方。我记得我加入的时候大概有 500 人。我当时担心的一件事是，我在寻找更早期的阶段，想知道这里是否足够有创业公司的感觉。但我加入之后就觉得，天哪，这里比我能想象的还要有创业味道。而且这一点即使到现在也没有变。那种自下而上的野心水平，以及任何人能够做任何事、拥有一个想法并把它发布的自由度，真的非常酷。但在使命方面，真正吸引我的是这个使命：把前沿智能带给每个人——构建 AGI（通用人工智能），然后把它带给每个人。而且我认为即使在当时，我们也意识到这个愿景不会是线性发展的。我们可能会尝试不同的产品，会有成功也有失败。但愿景没有变，使命没有变，我们开始看到各个部分逐渐拼合在一起。这真的非常酷。

turns.en: You worked on enterprise. A lot of people never touched ChatGPT Enterprise, God. What is something you learned there that you're bringing into your work now?
turns.zh: 你之前做过企业级产品。很多人从来没接触过 ChatGPT Enterprise，天哪。你从那里学到了什么，现在又带进了你当前的工作中？

turns.en: I think there's no one-size-fits-all solution in enterprise. I remember in the early days of ChatGPT Enterprise, we would talk to customers—this was about a year after ChatGPT was released—and everyone was so excited to bring AI into their enterprise. There were all these teams being set up as AI deployment teams with enormous budgets. If you asked anyone what they were excited about, or what they were excited to solve, at first you'd get the baseline answers: 'Yeah, we have all these contacts and data and all this stuff.' But then if you asked them what was a discrete use case they wanted AI to enable in their workplace, you'd get such a variance—an explosion of different types of answers. It's interesting: with these models and products, you have a box and you can say anything to it, which is the magic. But on the flip side, it also means you don't know what to do with it. And in enterprise, a big part of that is meeting users where they are—what use cases are they trying to solve—and then actually teaching them how they can use AI to gain leverage there.
turns.zh: 我觉得在企业领域没有一个放之四海而皆准的解决方案。我记得在 ChatGPT Enterprise 早期，我们会和客户交流——那是在 ChatGPT 发布大约一年后——每个人都兴奋地想将 AI 引入他们的企业。有各种各样的团队被组建起来，作为 AI 部署团队，拥有巨额预算。如果你问任何人他们兴奋的是什么、他们想解决什么，一开始你会得到一些很基础的答案：‘是的，我们有这些联系人和数据，有这些东西。’但是如果你再问他们，一个具体的、他们希望 AI 在工作场所实现的用例是什么，你会得到各种各样的答案——简直是不同类型答案的大爆发。有趣的是：使用这些模型和产品，你面前有一个盒子，你可以对它说任何话，这就是魔法。但反过来，这也意味着你不知道该拿它做什么。在企业里，很大一部分工作就是真正站在用户的立场上——他们想解决哪些用例——然后实际教他们如何用 AI 在那里获得杠杆。

turns.en: Do you meaningfully differentiate that from forward deployed engineering? Or—
turns.zh: 你有意把它和 forward deployed engineering（前沿部署工程）区分开吗？还是——

turns.en: I think there's the go-to-market side of it, and then there's the product side of it.
turns.zh: 我觉得这里面有 go-to-market（市场推广）的一面，也有产品的一面。

turns.en: I think—
turns.zh: 我觉得——

turns.en: You need to be more on the product side, yeah. And I think however good we get at the FDE motion, at the end of the day if we have a user looking at their computer or looking at their phone, it's our job in the product to enable them and show them where to go.
turns.zh: 你需要在产品方面更深入，是的。而且我觉得不管我们在 FDE（前沿部署工程）执行上做得多好，归根结底，如果有一个用户看着他们的电脑或手机，作为产品，我们的工作就是赋能他们、告诉他们该往哪走。

turns.en: So we're really excited about that.
turns.zh: 所以我们对此感到非常兴奋。

turns.en: Do you think there have been changes in adoption over the past three years? With step-function changes, reasoning models and so on, do enterprises still see AI as a black box and not know what to do with it, or have things changed?
turns.zh: 你觉得过去三年的采用情况有变化吗？随着阶跃式变化、推理模型等出现，企业是否仍然把 AI 视为黑盒、不知道如何运用？还是说情况已经改变了？

turns.en: We're seeing a huge uptick now. Everyone is extremely excited about it. It feels like hundreds of millions of people are using ChatGPT and understand generally how to work with AI. But every time a new capability gets unlocked — like what we're seeing with agents — there's probably still a contingent of early adopters who truly get it. They understand that you can do anything: you just have to make sure the right context is there, it's connected to the right tools, and you're supervising it. But then there's a market that's 10x or 100x bigger that doesn't see that yet. So I think that's the next stage here. To answer your question, adoption is there and growing fast, but the opportunity is far, far bigger. That's where we want to play, especially with ChatGPT Work.
turns.zh: 我们现在看到采用量大幅上升。每个人都非常兴奋。感觉有数亿人在使用 ChatGPT，并且大致知道如何与 AI 协作。但每当一个新能力被解锁——比如我们现在看到的智能体——可能仍只有一小部分早期采用者真正理解它。他们知道你可以做任何事情：只要确保有正确的上下文、连接到正确的工具，并且你在监督它，一切皆有可能。但还有 10 倍甚至 100 倍大的市场，他们还没理解，也还没看到这一点。所以我认为这就是下一阶段。回答你的问题：采用已经存在，而且在快速增长，但机会远比这大得多。这就是我们想要发力的地方，尤其是通过 ChatGPT Work。

turns.en: Let's skip ahead to ChatGPT Work. It was announced only about a month ago. What was the decision process that led into it? There was this overall merging into a super app — is that what we're officially calling it? You also deprecated the browser. Could you summarize the last couple of months of working on this?
turns.zh: 我们直接跳到 ChatGPT Work 吧。它大约一个月前才发布。是什么决策过程促成了这件事？整体上要合并成一个超级应用——这是官方叫法吗？你们还下架了浏览器。能概括一下你过去几个月在这个项目上的工作吗？

turns.en: Yeah, it feels like forever now, but I guess it's only been a few months. The most salient impetus, I think, was when we released Codex — or even just had it internally. It was really surprising to us. We recently put out some stats on this, but there was a real inflection in adoption among non-developers at OpenAI. Through the product development process, we run UX research sessions to talk to people internally. The thing that stuck out to me: you go talk to strategic finance, marketing, whatever, and they're all using Codex for their use cases. That part is cool. But the thing that really stood out was how proud people were that they were using Codex — like...
turns.zh: 是啊，感觉已经很久了，但其实只有几个月。我觉得最突出的推动力是当我们发布 Codex——甚至只是在内部使用 Codex 时。我们真的很惊讶。我们最近发布了一些数据，但 OpenAI 内部非开发者的采用确实出现了拐点。在产品开发过程中，我们会进行用户体验研究，和内部员工交流。让我印象最深的是：你去跟战略财务、市场部等的人聊，他们都在用 Codex 处理自己的用例，这很酷。但真正让我触动的是，大家为自己在使用 Codex 而感到自豪——就像……

turns.en: It's like, "I'm not supposed to be using it, but I am."
turns.zh: 就像在说“我不该用它，但我用了”。

turns.en: It was that they were early to this new thing, but also that they felt like they had a superpower. What we recognized then was: the power of Codex — the power of agents — could reach the massive distribution base of people who have come to know and love ChatGPT. How do we show that to them? How do we bring it to them? That's a hard product problem, and there are many ways to approach it. So that's what led to the merge, and over time the super app, and ultimately launching it in ChatGPT Work. But it came from that initial realization that this power was not only for developers — much earlier than we probably thought, it could be extended to everyone.
turns.zh: 那是他们很早就接触了这个新事物，同时也觉得他们拥有了一种超能力。我们当时意识到的是：Codex 的力量——智能体的力量——可以触达那些已经认识并喜爱 ChatGPT 的庞大用户基础。我们怎么把它展示给他们？怎么把它交到他们手里？这是一个很难的产品问题，也有很多种方法。所以这才促成了合并，最终形成了超级应用，并在 ChatGPT Work 中推出。但这个决定源于一个最初的认知：这种能力不仅仅属于开发者——比我们预想的更早，它可以扩展到所有人。

turns.en: How do you see the products differently? Who is it for? Codex started out as a CLI, then an app, now there's a merge of ChatGPT, Codex, and ChatGPT Work. Is it the opening for the average user, for enterprise, for work? How do you position it?
turns.zh: 你怎么看待这些产品的不同定位？它们是给谁用的？Codex 最初是命令行工具，后来是应用，现在 ChatGPT、Codex 和 ChatGPT Work 合并了。这是面向普通用户、企业还是工作场景的入口？你如何定位它？

turns.en: I think we want to position it for if you're doing work-like things.
turns.zh: 我认为我们希望把它定位为处理与工作相关的事情。

turns.en: Lack of a better word, right?
turns.zh: 找不到更好的词，对吧？

turns.en:
I think productivity is actually the pillar I support — that's the name of the team. The reason we call it productivity and not enterprise, or work, is because there's also personal productivity. With ChatGPT Work, I've seen people do things in their personal lives that you wouldn't technically classify as work, but these agents are super capable. One recent example someone posted on our Slack: someone had a missed package — they didn't receive it, but they got a photo of it from Amazon or whichever courier. They asked ChatGPT Work to find out where the package was. The agent was extremely tenacious: it took the image, looked at a bunch of listings around their neighborhood, and figured out exactly which apartment complex the package was in. So there are all these work-like or productivity-related things. That's what we want the product to be.

You asked about Codex. We think Codex is a durable brand, but we have a principle: we don't want a user to get stuck in a tab or an experience where they don't get the power of the product. So basically everything you can do in the Codex version of the product on desktop, you can do in ChatGPT Work, and vice versa. But we made some opinionated product decisions — for example, how much of the git state of a repo we expose to the end user, or how much we want to make the experience of seeing the agent's thinking and diffs forward such that you're exposed to the diff side of the button. On the safety side, we think about sandboxing and making sure we have the right defaults in one state versus the other. So there are opinions behind that, but we don't want the user to need to choose which experience they're in.
turns.zh:
我认为 Productivity（生产力）实际上是我所支持的支柱——这也是团队的名字。我们之所以叫它生产力，而不叫企业或工作，是因为还有个人生产力。就 ChatGPT Work 而言，我看到过人们在个人生活中做一些技术上不算工作的事情，但这些智能体也非常能干。最近有人在我们的 Slack 上分享了一个例子：有人有一个未收到的包裹——他没收到，但从亚马逊或某个快递公司那里得到了一张照片。他让 ChatGPT Work 找出包裹在哪里。这个智能体非常执着：它拿过图片，查看了他们小区附近的大量房源信息，最后确定了包裹所在的具体公寓楼。所以有所有这些类似工作或与生产力相关的事情。这就是我们希望产品成为的样子。

你问到 Codex。我们认为 Codex 是一个持久的品牌，但我们有一个原则：我们不希望用户被困在某个标签页或体验中，而无法获得产品的全部能力。所以基本上你在桌面版 Codex 产品中能做的所有事情，在 ChatGPT Work 中也能做，反之亦然。但我们做了一些有主见的产品决策——比如，我们要向终端用户暴露多少仓库的 git 状态；或者我们希望让用户看到智能体的思考过程和代码差异，以至于你总能看到按钮背后的 diff。在安全方面，我们考虑沙箱化，并确保在一个状态与另一个状态之间有正确的默认设置。所以背后有一些观点，但我们不希望用户需要选择自己处于哪种体验。

turns.en: That is a good goal for AGI — people don't want to have to choose what version of AGI they want; they just want the AGI to decide for them. Can I get an answer? It's not super clear to me: are the Codex harness and the ChatGPT Work harness the same? Is it just UI affordances, or are there actually prompt-level or even deeper differences?
turns.zh: 这对 AGI 来说是一个很好的目标——人们不想选择他们想要哪个版本的 AGI，他们只希望 AGI 替他们决定。我能得到一个答案吗？我还不完全清楚：Codex 的 harness 和 ChatGPT Work 的 harness 是一样的吗？只是 UI 上的差异，还是真的有提示词层面甚至更深的区别？

turns.en: The harness is the same — it's shared. In both products, we made improvements to the harness to make it good for knowledge work, especially as it relates to plugins, computer use, or artifacts. You get that power regardless of which experience you're in. On the UX side, we have opinionated takes: when you're in Codex mode, there's a specific view of what the UX should be and how it should behave.
turns.zh: Harness 是相同的——它是共享的。在这两个产品中，我们对 harness 进行了改进，使其适合知识工作，尤其是在插件、计算机使用或人工制品（artifacts）方面。无论你处于哪种体验中，你都能获得这种能力。在 UX 方面，我们有自己明确的观点：当你处于 Codex 模式时，我们对 UX 应该是什么样子以及应该如何表现有特定的看法。

transcript.sec: Motion vs. progress and closing remarks

turns.en: I think motion is much easier now than ever before because of the tooling that we have. But progress requires you to be very prescriptive and deliberate about what you're actually trying to achieve. And it goes back to our question of measurement. Like you were talking about whether we at OpenAI can figure out how to measure productivity for our users. That's a very hard problem because of the diversity, but as a team you should have a really prescriptive and deliberate view on what progress looks like for you and for your team. And if you don't have that, then it's very easy to conflate these two things.
turns.zh: 我认为，由于我们现在拥有的工具，行动比以往任何时候都容易得多。但进展要求你对实际想要达成的目标非常明确且审慎。这就回到了我们关于衡量的问题。比如你刚才谈到，我们 OpenAI 能否为我们的用户衡量生产力。因为用户的多样性，这是个非常难的问题，但作为一个团队，你应该对你自己和团队的进展形态有一个非常明确且审慎的看法。如果没有这种看法，就很容易把这两件事混为一谈。

turns.en: I think that's a really great thing. I'm really glad I like the discussion between motion and progress. I think that's a quote that we're going to feature in the write-up. You've been very generous with your time. Thank you so much, and congrats on 10 million.
turns.zh: 我觉得这真的很棒。我很高兴我喜欢关于行动与进展的这段讨论。我想我们会在文章里引用这句话。你真的很慷慨地抽出了时间。非常感谢，并恭喜你达到 1000 万。

turns.en: Yeah, thank you for having me.
